Select an email in your email list, then select .

Add an email attachment in Mail on iCloud.com

You can attach one or more files to an email.

Tip: You can also share files with other iCloud users through iCloud Drive. See Share files and folders in iCloud Drive on iCloud.com.

Add an attachment

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

While writing an email, select  in the top-right corner of the email window.

Tip: You can also drag the file directly into the email.

Choose to attach your file from iCloud Drive, iCloud Photos, or your device.

If you’re using a phone or tablet and choose your device, you can choose Photo Library, Take Photo or Video, or Choose Files.

Select the files you want to attach, then select Attach, Add, or Open; or take a photo or video, then tap Use Photo or Use Video.

If your attachments are too large to send in an email, you’re asked if you want to deliver the attachments using Mail Drop.

Note: If you send an email with large attachments, it might be returned by the recipient’s email service if your email exceeds the size limit set by that service.

Remove an attachment

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

While writing an email, do one of the following:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit next to the attachments section in the email window.

On a computer: Hold the pointer over the attachment in the email window.

Select .

You can only remove an attachment before you send the email.

You can’t remove files already sent with Mail Drop. They expire after 30 days.

Turn on Mail Drop for large attachments

You can use Mail Drop to upload large attachments to iCloud, where they’re encrypted. Recipients see an attachment or a Mail Drop link in the email, and they can download the files for up to 30 days after they’re sent. See the Apple Support article Mail Drop limits.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Composing in the sidebar, then select “Use Mail Drop when sending large attachments.”

See Reply to or forward email to include original attachments in a reply.

Save and find email addresses in Mail on iCloud.com

Set up an automatic reply in Mail on iCloud.com

You can set up an automatic reply to respond to incoming emails. You can use this feature even if you forward your iCloud Mail to another email account.

Send an automatic reply

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Auto-Reply in the sidebar.

Select the “Automatically reply to messages when they are received” checkbox, then type the message you want to send.

Set an optional date range.

The autoreply is active from the first day of the date range until the last.

Anyone who sends you multiple emails while you’re away receives one autoreply in a 24-hour period.

Stop sending an automatic reply

If you don’t set a date range when you set up your autoreply, you can turn it off manually.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Auto-Reply in the sidebar, then deselect the “Automatically reply to messages when they are received” checkbox.

Important: If you run out of iCloud storage, you won’t receive new emails. If you’re going to be away from your email for a while, make sure you have space available for new emails.

Read email in Mail on iCloud.com

You can view mail sent to your @icloud.com email address and any aliases in Mail on iCloud.com. If you have iCloud+, you can also view mail sent to your custom email domain addresses.

Note: Custom Email Domain isn’t available in all countries or regions.

Read an email

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Inbox in the Mailboxes list.

If you want to see a list of emails in a different mail folder, select that folder instead. For example, select Sent to see a list of emails you sent.

Select the email in your email list.

In your email list, emails are labeled with the following icons:

Icon

	

Description



	

An email is unread.



	

An email contains an attachment. See Download email attachments from Mail on iCloud.com.

An email that you flagged. See Search, filter, and flag email in Mail on iCloud.com.

Check for new emails

Your emails are updated automatically, but you can also manually refresh them.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list.

Mark an email as unread

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the email or emails you want to mark as unread in your email list:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Mark or , then select Mark as Unread.

Tip: If you’re using a computer, you can also hold your pointer over an email in the email list, click , then choose Mark as Unread.

Show the number of all unread messages on the Mail app icon

If you have categories turned on, the badge count for the Mail app reflects the number of unread messages in your Primary category. You can choose to show the total number of unread messages in all categories instead.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Categories in the sidebar, go to Badge Count, then select All Unread Messages.

If you can’t read an email because it’s encrypted, open it from one of your trusted devices. See What is a digitally signed and encrypted email?

Automatically forward email in Mail on iCloud.com

You can have all your iCloud Mail emails forwarded automatically to another email account. You may find this helpful if you use several email accounts.

If you set up a custom email domain for iCloud Mail, mail sent to your custom domain addresses will be forwarded as well.

Automatically forward email

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Mail Forwarding in the sidebar.

Select the “Forward my email to” checkbox, then type the forwarding address in the text field.

If you don’t want to store a copy of each forwarded email in iCloud, select the “Delete messages after forwarding” checkbox.

Keep in mind that storing copies of forwarded emails decreases your available iCloud storage space.

You can also specify criteria so that only certain emails are forwarded. When you set up a rule to forward certain emails to another account, you can only use one forwarding address for each rule. See Set up rules to filter email in Mail on iCloud.com.

Stop forwarding email

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Mail Forwarding in the sidebar, then deselect the “Forward my email to” checkbox.

Manage junk mail in Mail on iCloud.com

Most junk mail (spam) sent to your @icloud.com address or its aliases is automatically identified and moved to your Junk folder. If you receive unwanted email, you can manually mark it as junk.

Important: Because emails in the Junk folder are automatically deleted after 30 days, periodically check the Junk folder for emails that were mistakenly marked as junk.

Mark an email as junk

If iCloud Mail fails to mark an email as junk, you can manually move it from your inbox to the Junk folder.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the email or emails you want to mark as junk in your email list:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Mark or , then choose Move to Junk.

Subsequent emails from the same sender are automatically marked as junk.

Tip: If you’re using a computer, you can also hold your pointer over an email in the email list, click , then choose Move to Junk.

Indicate that an email isn’t junk

If iCloud Mail incorrectly marks an email as junk, you can manually move it from the Junk folder to your inbox.

Note: Emails from people in your iCloud contacts, or from recent conversations, won’t go to the Junk folder.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the Junk folder in the Mailboxes list.

Select the email or emails you want to indicate aren’t junk:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Mark or , then choose Move to Inbox.

Subsequent emails from the same sender will no longer be marked as junk.

Empty the Junk mailbox

You can delete all the emails in the Junk mailbox at the same time.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list.

Choose Empty Junk, then select Empty Junk again.

You can also delete individual emails in the Junk mailbox. See Delete email in Mail on iCloud.com.

Delete email in Mail on iCloud.com

Deleted emails are moved to the Trash mailbox. When you delete an email, it’s saved in your Trash for 30 days, after which it’s permanently erased. When you delete an email from iCloud.com, it’s deleted on all your devices that have Mail turned on in iCloud settings.

You can also change where your deleted emails are stored.

Important: If you view iCloud Mail in another app (for example, the Mail app on your iPhone or iPad), your mail might be deleted sooner than 30 days depending on the app’s settings.

Delete emails

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the email or emails you want to delete in your email list:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Trash or .

If you see  or Archive, you have “Show Archive icon in the toolbar” selected in Mail settings. See Archive email in Mail on iCloud.com. To delete an email or emails, select  or Move, then choose Trash.

Empty the Trash

You can delete all the emails in the Trash at the same time.

Important: When you empty the Trash, the emails are permanently deleted. You can’t recover them.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list.

Choose Empty Trash, then select Empty Trash again.

Erase emails immediately and permanently

You can set iCloud Mail to permanently and immediately erase emails when you delete them, instead of moving them to the Trash.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Mailbox Behavior in the sidebar, then deselect the “Move deleted messages to” checkbox.

Change the location of deleted emails

By default, emails in iCloud Mail are moved to the Trash when you delete them. You can change the folder they’re moved to.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Mailbox Behavior in the sidebar.

Select the “Move deleted messages to” checkbox, then select the current folder.

Choose another folder or select  to create a new folder, then select Done.

To delete Mail folders, see Organize email with folders in Mail on iCloud.com.

Use categories in Mail on iCloud.com

Mail can automatically sort your email messages into categories to help you find and manage them more quickly.

Primary: Find personal messages, direct communications, and time-sensitive information.

Transactions: Keep track of your confirmations, receipts, and shipping notices.

Updates: Catch up on news, newsletters, and social updates.

Promotions: Browse your marketing, coupons, and sale messages.

When an email in Transactions, Updates, or Promotions includes time-sensitive information, it’s also included in the Primary email list.

Note: Mail categories may not be available in all languages.

Turn on Mail categories

You can turn on categorization when you first open Mail on iCloud.com. If you choose Not Now, you can also turn it on later in Settings.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Categories in the sidebar, then select Turn On Categorization.

If categorization is turned on but the categories aren’t visible, select , then select Show Categories.

Change the category of a sender

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a message, then select  at the top.

Choose Categorize, then choose a specific category or choose to automatically categorize messages.

Select Save.

Your choice applies to all current and future messages from the sender.

If you’re using a computer, you can also recategorize messages by dragging them to another category in the sidebar.

Recategorize all of your messages automatically

You can reset your preferences so all messages are automatically categorized into Primary, Transactions, Updates, and Promotions. This setting undoes any manual categorization.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Categories in the sidebar, then select Reset Manual Categorization.

View and manage all categorized messages from a sender

When you select a Transactions, Updates, or Promotions message, a digest view of messages from that sender opens. For example, if you open a Transactions message, all of the other Transactions messages from that sender appear when you scroll up or down.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Transactions, Updates, or Promotions in the Mailboxes list, then select a message.

All of your messages from the sender in that category appear in a list.

To view all of your messages from a sender, select  at the top of the sender’s email list, then choose All Messages.

To manage all of your messages from a sender, select  at the top, then choose to mark them as unread, move them to a folder, archive them, or delete them.

Note: Primary messages aren’t grouped by sender.

To view only one Transactions, Updates, or Promotions thread when scrolling, select , then select Group By Thread.

Remove time-sensitive messages from the Primary category

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Primary in the Mailboxes list, then select a message.

Select  at the top, then choose Don’t Show In Primary.

Turn off Mail categories

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list.

Do one of the following:

Turn off the categories view: Select Hide Categories.

You can easily hide and show the categories without losing categorization information.

Turn off categorization: Select Settings, select Categories in the sidebar, then select Turn Off Categorization.

Future messages aren’t sorted into categories.

Automatically clean up your iCloud Mail inbox on iCloud.com

Mail can help you keep your inbox uncluttered and free up storage by deleting old promotions, unsubscribing from mailing lists in bulk, and more. When you set up iCloud Mail Cleanup recommendations, they work on any device that has iCloud Mail turned on.

Note: iCloud Mail Cleanup may not be available in all languages.

Turn on iCloud Mail Cleanup

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Cleanup Recommendations at the bottom of the Mailboxes list.

Select Get Recommendations, then select Done.

Your inbox isn’t affected until you turn on a cleanup recommendation. See Turn on a cleanup recommendation.

You can also turn on iCloud Mail Cleanup on your iPhone or iPad. See Automatically clean up your iCloud Mail inbox on iPhone or Automatically clean up your iCloud Mail inbox on iPad.

Turn on a cleanup recommendation

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select iCloud Mail Cleanup at the bottom of the Mailboxes list, then select .

Note: You may also see unsubscribe recommendations after you’ve received enough messages in the Promotions and Updates categories.

Select one of the recommendations. For example, you can choose Clean Up Old Promotions or Archive Old Transactions.

If necessary, select the pop-up menu for a rule, then choose another option.

Action: What happens to the email

Status: Whether the action applies to unread emails, read emails, or all emails

Age: How old the emails need to be before the action applies

Tip: You can edit the rules at any point by selecting the recommendation, making changes, then selecting Save.

Select Turn On.

Delete a cleanup recommendation

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select iCloud Mail Cleanup at the bottom of the Mailboxes list, then select .

Select the recommendation you want to turn off, select Delete Rule, then select Delete.

Unsubscribe from a sender in Updates and Promotions

Use iCloud Mail Cleanup to unsubscribe from a sender in the Updates and Promotions categories, and automatically move future messages to the Trash.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select an email in the Updates or Promotions category.

Select  in the bottom-right corner of the email, then select Unsubscribe.

Select Unsubscribe again.

Use iCloud Mail Cleanup recommendations to unsubscribe

iCloud Mail Cleanup can recommend senders in the Updates and Promotions categories to unsubscribe from in bulk, and automatically move future messages to the Trash.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select iCloud Mail Cleanup at the bottom of the Mailboxes list, then select .

Select Unsubscribed, then select Unsubscribe Recommendations.

Select each sender you want to unsubscribe from, then select Unsubscribe from [X] Senders.

Note: If you don’t see any recommendations, iCloud Mail Cleanup doesn’t have any recommendations at this time.

Remove a sender from the Unsubscribed list

If you change your mind and want to receive emails from a sender you unsubscribed from, you can remove them from the Unsubscribed list.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select iCloud Mail Cleanup at the bottom of the Mailboxes list, then select .

Select Unsubscribed, then select Edit next to Senders.

Select  next to each sender you want to remove from the Unsubscribed list, then select Done.

To receive emails again from a sender you were previously unsubscribed from, you can sign up for updates and promotions through their website again. After you resubscribe, future messages from that sender will go to your inbox.

Turn off iCloud Mail Cleanup

When you turn off iCloud Mail Cleanup, iCloud Mail stops managing old messages. It also deletes the list of any senders you unsubscribed from and stops deleting their messages.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select iCloud Mail Cleanup at the bottom of the Mailboxes list, then select .

Select Turn Off iCloud Mail Cleanup, then select Turn Off iCloud Mail Cleanup again.

Organize email with folders in Mail on iCloud.com

iCloud includes seven default Mail folders: Inbox, VIP, Drafts, Sent, Archive, Trash, and Junk. You can create additional folders and subfolders to organize your email.

When you create folders, they’re visible on any device that has Mail turned on in iCloud settings.

To work with folders, make sure the Mailboxes list is visible.

Create a folder or subfolder

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do one of the following:

Create a new folder: While a default folder is selected, select  next to Folders in the Mailboxes list. Type a name, then tap or press Return or Enter.

Create a subfolder: Select the folder where you want to add a subfolder, select , type the new subfolder’s name, then tap or press Return or Enter.

If you’re using a computer, you can also click an existing folder and drag it onto another folder.

The folders you create are sorted alphabetically.

Rename or delete a folder

Important: Deleting a folder deletes everything inside it—emails, subfolders, and emails in subfolders.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Tap or double-click the name of the folder you want to rename or delete.

If you’re using a phone or tablet, you may have to tap Edit first.

Do one of the following:

Rename a folder: Type the folder’s new name, then tap or press Return or Enter.

Delete a folder: Select  to the left of the folder’s name, then select Delete.

Move email into a folder

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the email or emails you want to move in your email list:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Move , choose a folder or create a new folder, then select Move.

If you’re using a computer, you can also select one or more emails, then drag them onto a folder in the Mailboxes list.

Search, filter, and flag email in Mail on iCloud.com

There are many ways you can locate emails in Mail on iCloud.com. You can search and filter mail in a mailbox or folder. You can also flag important emails.

Search for emails

You can search all emails within a mailbox or folder.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the folder you want to search in the Mailboxes list.

Tap  or click in the search field above the email list, then type the text you want to find.

You can do any of the following:

Search within a field: After you type a term, choose a suggestion below the search field, such as “Sender contains” or “Subject contains.”

Enter multiple search terms: Type a term, tap or press Return or Enter, then type another term.

Search unread emails: Start typing the word “unread,” then choose the “Message is unread” suggestion.

Search for email from a particular time period: Start typing a date or time period, such as “2022” or “last week,” then choose a date suggestion.

When the search field is empty, you see a list of previous searches.

To exit the search and see all your emails again, delete the text in the search field or select Cancel.

Filter email

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the folder you want to filter in the Mailboxes list.

Tip: You can filter emails deleted by iCloud Mail Cleanup in the Trash folder.

Select  above the email list.

You can see the current filter next to “Filtered by.”

Do one of the following:

Change the filter: Select the current filter. In the pop-up menu, choose the filter or filters you want to use.

Stop filtering emails: Select  again.

You can also filter emails on the iCloud.com homepage. Select  in the lower-right corner of the tile, turn it on, then select a filter.

Flag important emails

Flagged emails are displayed with a flag icon . You can filter emails in a folder to show only those that are flagged.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the email or emails you want to flag in your email list:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Edit at the top of the email list, then tap  next to the email or emails.

On a computer: Click the email. To select multiple emails, Command-click (on a Mac) or Control-click (on a Windows device) the emails.

Select Mark or , then choose Flag.

Tip: You can also flag individual emails in a conversation. Select  in the bottom-right corner of the email, then choose Flag.

Set up rules to filter email in Mail on iCloud.com

You can set up rules to filter incoming emails or reorganize emails you’ve already received. For example, you can create a rule that sorts emails from a particular sender into a specific folder. You can edit and delete these rules at any time.

Set up rules to filter email

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Rules in the sidebar, then select  in the top-right corner.

Enter a name for the new rule.

Below Message, use the pop-up menu and text field to specify the type of emails you want to filter.

Below Action, use the pop-up menu or field to specify an action for the rule.

Select Add.

You can have up to 500 rules.

Important: If you apply rules to a folder and then delete the folder or change its name, make sure to update the rules for those folders accordingly. For example, you can’t forward emails to a deleted folder.

Change or delete email filtering rules

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Rules in the sidebar, then select a rule.

Do any of the following:

Change a rule: Specify new filtering conditions in the pop-up menus and text fields, then select Save Changes.

Delete a rule: Select Delete.

Reorder email filtering rules

When you have multiple rules, they’re applied in the order in which they appear in the list.

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Rules in the sidebar, then drag a rule up or down in the list.

Note: It may take up to 15 minutes for new or changed rules to take effect on incoming emails.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note with a table.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

In the row or column you want to work with, tap or click a cell.

To select a row, select  to the left of the row; to select a column, select  above the column.

On a phone or tablet, tap an option. On a computer, first click , then choose an option.

Organize notes in folders on iCloud.com

You can create folders to keep your notes organized. You can create your own folders, and Notes creates the following folders automatically:

All iCloud: Shows notes from all folders except the Recently Deleted folder.

Notes: Contains notes that you haven’t moved to folders you created or aren’t in the Recently Deleted folder.

Recently Deleted: Contains notes you deleted in the last 30 days.

Create a folder

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select New Folder at the bottom of the folder list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

Name the folder, then press Return or Enter.

Your folder appears alphabetically in the folder list.

Tip: You can also create a new folder in an existing folder. Select  next to the folder where you want to add a subfolder. (On a computer, hold your pointer over the folder until  appears.) Then choose New Folder.

Rename a folder

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  next to the folder you want to rename. (On a computer, hold your pointer over the folder until  appears.)

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

Select Rename Folder, add a new name, then press Return or Enter.

Your folder appears alphabetically in the folder list.

Delete a folder

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  next to the folder you want to delete. (On a computer, hold your pointer over the folder until  appears.)

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

Select Delete Folder.

Notes in the folder you delete are moved to the Recently Deleted folder, where they remain for 30 days. During that time you can still view and recover them. After 30 days, notes are permanently removed from iCloud.com and any Apple devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. See Delete and recover notes on iCloud.com.

You can’t delete the All iCloud, Notes, or Recently Deleted folders, but you can delete notes in them. If you delete all the notes in the Recently Deleted folder, it disappears until you delete more notes.

Move a folder or note from one folder to another

You need to be on a computer to move a folder or note.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Drag a note or folder to another folder.

When you move a note or folder to a new folder, the note automatically takes on the sharing permissions of that folder. For example, if you move a note to a shared folder, the note is then shared. If you move a note out of a shared folder, the note is no longer shared. See Share folders in Notes on iCloud.com.

You can’t move notes to the All iCloud folder.

Tip: To move a subfolder to the top level of the folder list, drag and drop the subfolder to the All iCloud folder.

Organize your notes with tags and pins on iCloud.com

You can use tags as a fast and flexible way to categorize and organize your notes. You can add one or more tags to a note, such as #shopping and #work, and easily filter your notes across folders using the Tag Browser.

On a computer, you can also pin your most important notes to the top of the notes list for easy access.

Add tags to notes

You can type a tag anywhere in a note. Tags must be a single word, but you can use hyphens and underscores (for example, #meeting-minutes or #important_documents).

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Type the number sign (#), then type a word—for example, #meeting or #important—or choose from the list of suggested tags. (Suggested tags appear if you already added tags in Notes.)

Tags you add appear in the Tag Browser in the sidebar.

If you add a tag to a shared note, it appears as dimmed text to other participants who don’t have the tag in their Tag Browser.

View notes with tags

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

To see a list of notes that contain a tag, select the tag in the Tag Browser in the sidebar or folder list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

You can select multiple tags to see a list of notes that contain those tags.

Pin notes

You need to be on a computer to pin notes.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Control-click (on a Mac) or right-click (on a Windows device) the note you want to pin, then choose Pin Note.

To unpin a note, Control-click (on a Mac) or right-click (on a Windows device) the note you want to unpin, then choose Unpin Note.

View notes and locked notes on iCloud.com

When you set up Notes with iCloud, your notes stay up to date on iCloud.com and every device with Notes turned on in iCloud settings.

The notes list contains the notes in the currently selected folder. Notes are listed by last-modified date, with the most recent note at the top of the notes list. The list shows the first few words of each note.

View a note

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note in the list. You may need to select a different folder to see the note you’re looking for.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

View and close locked notes

You can view notes you locked on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account.

Note: If you locked your notes with your Apple device’s passcode or login password, you can’t view them on iCloud.com.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a locked note in the list, then enter the password you created for locked notes.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

After you enter the password for one locked note, you can view other locked notes without reentering the password. The notes are locked again after a period of inactivity or when you close the browser window.

Important: If you reset the Notes password using Notes on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac, entering the new Notes password only lets you view locked notes that use the new password. If some of your notes use an older password, you must enter that password to view them.

To close a locked note, select  in the Notes toolbar.

To add a lock to a note, remove a lock from a note, change the password for locked notes, or reset the password if you forget it, use the Notes app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. See the Apple Support article How to lock or unlock notes on your iPhone or iPad or Lock your notes on Mac in the Notes User Guide.

View or download attachments in Notes on iCloud.com

You can attach items to notes by using the Notes app on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac. You can then view and download those attachments—photos, audio files, maps, iWork files, and more—in Notes on iCloud.com, as long as you’re signed in to the same Apple Account.

View or play photos, audio files, maps, and other attachments

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note that contains the attachment you want to view or play.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Tap or double-click the attachment.

The attached content is downloaded to your device, opened in the relevant application, or both.

View and download scanned documents

If you have an iPhone or iPad and you scanned documents in the Notes app, you can view and download the documents in iCloud.com.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note that contains a scanned document.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Do either of the following:

View the document: Tap or double-click the thumbnail of the scanned document.

Download the document: Tap or double-click the thumbnail of the scanned document, then select .

To view and download another document, select its thumbnail in the Scanned Documents window.

View and edit attached iWork documents

You can view and edit Pages, Numbers, and Keynote documents you attached using the Notes app on devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account.

Note: You need to be on a computer to edit Pages, Numbers, and Keynote documents on iCloud.com.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a note that contains a Pages, Numbers, or Keynote attachment.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Tap or double-click the attachment. On a phone or tablet, choose if you want to View or Download.

A copy of the attachment is saved in iCloud Drive and opens in Pages on iCloud, Numbers on iCloud, or Keynote on iCloud. To learn more about iCloud Drive, see Use iCloud Drive on iCloud.com.

Important: Any changes you make only affect the copy of the document saved in iCloud Drive, and not the document attached to the note.

Note: In locked notes on iCloud.com, you see placeholders for attachments instead of the actual attachment content. To view attachments in locked notes, use the Notes app on a device where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account.

Delete and recover notes on iCloud.com

You can delete notes you no longer need. You can also recover recently deleted notes within 30 days.

Delete a note

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the note you want to delete.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Select  in the Notes toolbar.

When you delete a note, it’s moved to the Recently Deleted folder on iCloud.com and on your devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. You can view and recover notes in the Recently Deleted folder for up to 30 days before they’re permanently removed from all your devices. If you want to edit notes in the Recently Deleted folder, you must first recover them.

Recover recently deleted notes

You can recover and edit notes you deleted in the last 30 days on iCloud.com or on devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. However, you can’t recover notes you permanently removed.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Recently Deleted in the folder list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

If you don’t see Recently Deleted, you don’t have any notes in that folder, and there’s nothing to be recovered.

Select a note, then select Recover in the Notes toolbar.

The note moves to the Notes folder.

If you’re on a computer and you want to move a recovered note directly to a folder you created, drag the note from the Recently Deleted folder to another folder.

Note: If you delete a shared note that you don’t own, the note doesn’t move to your Recently Deleted folder. See Delete shared notes on iCloud.com.

Permanently remove deleted notes

You can immediately and permanently remove notes you deleted in the last 30 days on iCloud.com or on devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Recently Deleted in the folder list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

If you don’t see Recently Deleted, you don’t have any recently deleted notes.

Select a note you want to permanently remove, then select  in the Notes toolbar.

The selected note is removed immediately from all your devices.

Notes you leave in the Recently Deleted folder are automatically and permanently removed after 30 days.

To learn what happens when you delete a shared note and how to recover a deleted shared note, see Delete shared notes on iCloud.com.

Share notes on iCloud.com

You can invite people to view and edit a note. When you share a note, only people you invite can view and edit it, even if someone else has a link to the note.

Note: You can’t share a locked note.

When you share a note, the Shared icon  appears next to the note in the notes list, and when the note is selected, the View Participants button  is highlighted and shows a checkmark.

Note: You need to be on a tablet or computer to share folders and manage sharing; however, you can still make updates to shared folders and delete shared folders on a phone.

Share notes

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select or write the note you want to share.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Select  in the Notes toolbar.

Select a sharing option.

Email: Select Email, choose the permission level of the participants and whether they can add or remove other people, then select Share. In the window that appears, add email addresses in the To field, write an optional message, then select .

Copy Link: Select Copy Link, then add the email addresses or phone numbers of your participants. Choose their permission level and whether they can add or remove other people, then select Share.

Only the people you invite can view and edit the note.

Note: You can invite people using any email address or phone number, although participants need an Apple Account to view and edit a note.

Manage participants

The owner of a note can add and remove participants. Anyone who has been added to the note and given permission to add other people can also add and remove participants. Any participant can always remove themselves.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the shared note in the notes list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Select , then do any of the following:

Add participants: Select Add People at the bottom of the participants list. When a person has been invited but has not yet accepted, Invited appears under the person’s name.

Note: The image above shows Notes on iCloud.com on a computer. The appearance may vary slightly on a phone or tablet.

Manage permissions: Tap or hold the pointer over the person’s name, select , then choose whether the person can make changes or only view the note. You can also allow the person to add other people.

Remove participants: Tap or hold the pointer over the person’s name, then select  and choose Remove Access.

If you want to manage permissions on a note in a shared folder, you must adjust them at the folder level. In a note that’s in a shared folder, select  in the toolbar, then select Manage Shared Folders. See Share folders in Notes on iCloud.com.

Remove yourself from a shared note

If you’re a participant, you can remove yourself from a shared note.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the note you want to remove yourself from, then select .

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Tap or hold the pointer over your name, then select  and choose Remove Me.

Stop sharing notes

You must be the owner of a note to stop sharing it.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the note you want to stop sharing in the notes list.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see your notes, make sure the notes list is open.

Select , then do one of the following:

Stop sharing with all participants: Select Stop Sharing.

Stop sharing with just one participant: Tap or hold the pointer over the person’s name, then select  and choose Remove Access.

If you share a folder, all of the notes in that folder automatically take on the sharing permissions of that folder. See Share folders in Notes on iCloud.com.

Share folders in Notes on iCloud.com

You can share a folder with one or more people. When you share the folder, all of the subfolders and notes within the folder are shared as well. Only the people you invite to the folder can view or edit its contents.

Note: You can’t share a folder that contains a locked note.

Manage participants in a shared folder

The owner of a folder can add and remove participants. Anyone who has been added to the note and given permission to add other people can also add and remove participants. Any participant can always remove themselves.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do any of the following:

Add participants: Select Add People at the bottom of the participants list. When a person has been invited but hasn’t yet accepted, Invited appears below the person’s name.

Manage permissions: Tap or hold the pointer over the person’s name, select , then choose whether the person can make changes or only view the folder. You can also allow the person to add other people.

Remove participants: Tap or hold the pointer over the person’s name, then select  and choose Remove Access.

Remove yourself from a shared folder

If you’re a participant, you can remove yourself from a shared folder.

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Go to icloud.com/notes, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

Edit the notes within the folder.

When someone makes an update to a shared folder or to the notes within a shared folder, everyone sharing the folder sees the changes, but no one can see who made them. If an edit is made to a note in a shared folder, the timestamp below the note in the notes list shows the last time it was edited. If you’re not currently editing a shared note, a yellow dot appears next to the note when someone else edits it.

If you were invited to edit a folder using an email address or phone number that isn’t associated with the Apple Account you use for iCloud, ask the owner to resend the invitation using the correct email address or phone number. You can also follow the onscreen instructions to associate that email address or phone number with your Apple Account.

If you’re on a phone or tablet and you don’t see the folder list, make sure the folder list is open.

Select Delete Folder.

One of the following happens:

If you’re the owner: The folder is removed from the devices of everyone you shared it with. You can recover recently deleted notes from your Recently Deleted folder.

Notes in the folder you delete are moved to the Recently Deleted folder, where they remain for 30 days. During that time you can still view and recover them. After 30 days, notes are permanently removed from iCloud.com and all devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. See Delete and recover notes on iCloud.com.

If you’re a participant: The folder is removed for you, but the owner and other participants can still access the shared folder and all of its content. View your photos and videos on iCloud.com

You can view photos and videos stored in iCloud Photos using a web browser.

View your photos and videos

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do one of the following:

Select Library in the sidebar to see thumbnails of all your photos and videos.

Select an album or folder in the sidebar to view its contents.

You can also switch between viewing your personal library, shared library, or both. See View your iCloud Shared Photo Library on iCloud.com.

View your photos and videos in full screen on a phone or tablet

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do any of of the following:

Enter full screen: Tap a thumbnail.

Move between photos or videos: Swipe left or right.

View or hide thumbnails at the bottom of the screen: Tap the photo.

Exit full screen: Tap Back in the top-left corner.

View your photos and videos in full screen on a computer

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do any of of the following:

Enter full screen: Double-click a photo thumbnail, then click .

Move between photos or videos: Press the arrow keys on your keyboard. You can also hold the pointer over the left or right side of a photo, then click the arrow that appears.

View or hide thumbnails at the bottom of the screen: Hold the pointer over the top of a photo, then click .

Exit full screen: Hold the pointer over the top of a photo, then click .

Change the shape of the photo and video thumbnails on a computer

On a computer, you can view the thumbnails of your photos and videos as squares (which eliminates the empty space between them) or in their original aspect ratio (which shows the entire image).

Note: On a phone or tablet, photos and videos are always shown as squares.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do one of the following:

View your images as squares: Click .

View your images in their original aspect ratio: Click .

Change the video playback quality

You can change the playback quality of the videos you view on iCloud.com.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

While viewing a video, do one of the following:

On a phone or tablet: Tap , then choose the quality setting. (If you’re playing a video in full screen, exit full screen, then tap ).

On a computer: Hold the pointer over the video, click , then choose the quality setting.

Videos on iCloud.com play at Medium quality by default. Your playback quality settings reset when you sign out.

View your memories

The Photos app recognizes significant people, places, and events in your library, and presents them in curated collections called Memories.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Memories in the sidebar.

At the top, select Favorite Memories to see memories you added to Favorites. Or select See All (on a phone or tablet) or Memories (on a computer) to see all of your memories.

Note: If you don’t see any memories, try opening them on your device first. See Watch memories in Photos in the iPhone User Guide.

Select a memory to play it.

While the memory plays, tap or hold the pointer over the memory, then do any of the following:

Pause: Select . To start playing again, select .

Restart the memory: Select  in the bottom-left corner.

See all the photos in the memory: On a phone or tablet, tap  in the top-right corner, then choose an option. On a computer, click  in the bottom-right corner.

View the memory full screen (only available on computers): Click  in the bottom-left corner. To exit full screen, click .

Stop watching the memory: Select  in the top-left corner.

You can also play your photos in a slideshow.

Find your photos and videos on iCloud.com

On iCloud.com, you can search for photos and videos in your photo library. You can also view photos and videos in your library, sorted by when they were taken. If you want to quickly view older photos, you can jump to a specific month and year.

Tip: You can find photos in the Photos app by searching for associated text, a keyword, or a date. See Find photos by text, content, or date in the Photos User Guide for Mac, and “Search for photos and videos” in the user guides for iPhone and iPad.

Search for photos and videos on iCloud.com

With iOS 26.4, iPadOS 26.4, macOS 26.4, or later, you can have a trusted device provide search results for your library in Photos on iCloud.com. Your searches are encrypted and no search history is kept on Apple servers by using on-device processing. When you type in the search field, you see suggestions of dates, people, provided by your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Library in the sidebar.

Type what you’re looking for in the search field, such as:

Date (month or year)

Place (city or state)

Business names (museums, for example)

Category (beach or sunset, for example)

Events (sports games or concerts, for example)

Text (an email address or phone number, for example)

Captions

Select one of the suggestions or press Return.

Select  to clear the search.

Note: If you haven’t turned on Allow Search on iCloud.com, you’re prompted to enable search using your trusted device. Select Continue, open the notification that appears on your device, then select Allow.

Browse your library by month and year

You can quickly go to a month and year in your personal library, your shared library, or both at the same time. See Switch between your personal library and shared library.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Library in the sidebar.

Select , choose a year, then choose a month.

Show other photos or videos in your library

You can’t browse your Favorites, Recents, or other albums by date. However, you can quickly find a photo or video in your library, which is sorted by when each photo was taken.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Recents or Favorites in the sidebar.

Select the photo or video you want to find.

Select , then choose Show in Library.

Only the person who added the photo or video to the shared library can permanently delete it. See Delete and recover photos and videos on iCloud.com.

Create and join shared albums in Photos on iCloud.com

You can use Shared Albums to share photos and videos with the people you choose—and they can add their own photos, videos, and comments.

For setup instructions, see Set up Shared Albums in iCloud on all your devices. To create an album that isn’t shared, see Organize photos and videos in albums.

Note: Not all features are available in all countries or regions.

Create a shared album

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Shared Albums in the sidebar, then select .

Enter a name for the new album, then do any of the following:

Choose who can access: Select People You Choose or Anyone with the Link. If you select People You Choose, you have the option to turn on Access Requests.

Make the album temporary: Turn on Make Album Temporary to set the album to expire after 30 days. After that time, any photos or videos in your temporary album not saved to your photo library will be deleted.

Temporary albums don’t count toward your iCloud storage.

Select Create.

Manage sharing for an album

If you’re the creator of a shared album, you control who can access it.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Shared Albums in the sidebar.

Tap or hold the pointer over a shared album, select , then choose Manage Shared Album.

If you see participants and access options, do any of the following:

Update access for a participant: Tap or hold the pointer over a participant’s name, select , then choose an option.

Remove a participant: Tap or hold the pointer over a participant’s name, select , then choose Remove Participant.

Change who can access: Select People You Choose or Anyone with the Link. If you select People You Choose, you can turn on Access Requests.

Approve or decline access requests: Below Requests, select an option next to the participant’s name.

Invite a person to join: Select Invite Participant, select Create Link, then copy and share the one-time link. Create a new link to invite more people.

Deactivate unused share links: If you share a link but no longer want that participant to join the album, select , then choose Remove Unused Share Links.

If you see Subscribers Can Post, do any of the following:

Allow people you invite to add to this album: Turn on Subscribers Can Post.

Allow anyone to view the album on iCloud.com: Turn on Public Website.

Tip: If Public Website is on, you can select Copy to copy the link to send it to people.

Invite more people: Select , enter one or more email addresses, then select Invite.

Remove a subscriber: Select  next to the subscriber’s name.

Join a shared album

Select the link you received, then select Join. You may need to ask for access, provide your email, or sign in to your Apple Account.

If you join by email and want to save the album to your account, sign in to your Apple Account.

Delete or leave a shared album

If you’re the creator of a shared album, you can delete it. If you’re a participant, you can leave it.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Shared Albums in the sidebar.

Tap or hold the pointer over a shared album, then select .

Select Manage Shared Album, then choose one of the following:

Delete Shared Album: The album is automatically removed from all of your devices and the devices of participants.

WARNING: Deleting a shared album permanently deletes all of its photos. Before continuing, make sure that you save any photos you want to keep.

Leave Shared Album: The album is automatically removed from only your device.

After you create a shared album, you can upload photos and videos.

On a phone or tablet: Tap  in the bottom-right corner, tap Download, then tap Download again.

Add star ratings, captions, keywords, and more in Photos on iCloud.com

In Photos on iCloud.com, you can view and edit metadata about a photo or video, such as the title, date, time, and location. You can also add captions, keywords, and star ratings to make it easier to search for items.

Add or edit the title, caption, location, and more

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Tap or double-click the photo or video you want to see more information about.

Select .

Title and caption: Enter text in the field.

Date and time: Select anything in the Adjusted field, then specify the new date or time. To discard any changes, select Revert to Original.

Location: Enter a location in the field, then choose an option. To remove the location, select Remove Location.

Select Save.

The title appears in the Photos toolbar when you view a photo. You can also see it from the thumbnail view.

Add or edit keywords

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Tap or double-click the photo or video you want to see more information about.

Select .

Select Add Keywords or Edit.

You can use the search field to find items by keyword if you allow Data Access and Search on iCloud.com.

Add or edit star ratings

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Tap or double-click the photo or video you want to see more information about.

Select .

Next to rating, select a number of stars, or select the current rating to remove it.

If you add or edit a caption, keyword, or star rating for an item in your iCloud Shared Photo Library, all participants see the changes.

Organize photos and videos in albums on iCloud.com

When you organize photos and videos in an album in Photos on iCloud.com, those changes appear on any of your devices that have iCloud Photos turned on.

Note: You can only organize photos and videos in your personal library on iCloud.com. To add an item from an iCloud Shared Photo Library to an album or view items that are already in an album, use the Photos app on a device with iOS 16.1, iPadOS 16, macOS 13, or later.

Create an album

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do one of the following:

On a phone or tablet: Tap Albums in the sidebar, tap , then tap New Album.

On a computer: Hold the pointer over Albums in the sidebar, click , then choose New Album.

Enter a name for the new album, then select Save.

To view the album, select Albums in the sidebar, then select the album name.

Add photos or videos to an album

You can add photos or videos to an album from your library on iCloud.com. If the photo or video is on your computer, you can upload it directly to the album.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the photos or videos you want to add to an album, then select .

Choose Add to Album, select an album, then select Add.

Tip: On a computer, you can also add photos and videos to an album by dragging them to the album in the sidebar.

Rename an album

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select an album in the sidebar.

Select the name at the top of the window, then type a new name.

If you’re using a phone or tablet, you may need to tap Edit first.

Remove photos and videos from an album

Deleting a photo or video from an album removes it from the album only. It still remains in Photos on iCloud.com and on any device that has iCloud Photos turned on.

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select an album in the sidebar to view its contents.

Select the photos or videos you want to remove, select , then select Remove.

Delete an album

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Albums in the sidebar.

Tap or hold the pointer over an album, select , then select Delete Album.

Select Delete.

The album is removed from iCloud Photos on all your devices, but the items in the album are still visible in your photo library and other albums that contain them.

If you want to create a shared album, see Create and join shared albums in Photos on iCloud.com.

Start a slideshow

Navigate a slideshow while it’s playing

Delete and recover photos and videos on iCloud.com

When you delete a photo or video from Photos on iCloud.com, it’s also deleted from all your devices that have iCloud Photos turned on. If you change your mind, you have 30 days to recover it before it’s permanently deleted.

About shared photos and videos

If you delete a photo or video in a shared album or a shared library, it’s deleted from the devices of all members. You also may not be able to delete photos and videos other people added:

Shared albums: If you’re the creator of a shared album, you can delete any photos, videos, or comments in the album. If you’re a subscriber, you can delete anything that you personally added.

Shared libraries: Any participant of a shared library can delete photos and videos. Only the person who added the photo or video to the shared library can permanently delete it before 30 days have passed.

Delete photos and videos

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the photos or videos you want to delete.

Select , then select Delete.

Deleted photos and videos are moved to the Recently Deleted album.

To permanently delete photos or videos before they’re automatically deleted, go to the Recently Deleted album, select the items you want to delete, then select Delete.

Recover photos and videos

Go to icloud.com/photos, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the Recently Deleted album in the sidebar.

Select the photos or videos you want to recover, then select Recover.

Create and delete reminders on iCloud.com

Each reminder you create is put in a reminder list.

Create a reminder

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select a list for the new reminder, then do one of the following:

If you’re using updated reminders, select  to add a reminder to the bottom of the list.

You can also add a reminder below an existing reminder. Select the title of the reminder, then tap or press Return or Enter.

If you’re not using updated reminders, select New Item.

Tip: To create a reminder from the iCloud.com homepage, select  in the corner of the Reminders tile. To create a new reminder from anywhere on iCloud.com, select  in the toolbar, then select Reminder.

Type the reminder (for example, “dentist appointment”) in the text field that appears, then tap or press Return or Enter.

Add details to a reminder for updated reminders

You can add details to a reminder, like a note or alert. You can edit the reminder’s title, add notes, set an alert for a day or location, and flag a reminder.

Note: If you’re using updated reminders, you can also view a note’s priority and list on iCloud.com. Use the Reminders app on a device with iOS 13, iPadOS 13, macOS 10.15, or later to add additional details.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the reminder you want to add details to, select , then do any of the following:

Edit the reminder title: Type a new title.

Add a note: Type a description or other information in the text field.

Receive an alert on a specific day: Turn on “Remind me on a Day,” then set the date and time.

Receive an alert at a particular location: Turn on Remind at Location, then select the pop-up menu and choose an option.

Flag a reminder: Select the flag at the top of the details pane.

Add details to a reminder (if you’re not using updated reminders)

If you’re not using updated reminders, you can add notes, set an alert for a specific day, and assign a priority to reminders.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the reminder you want to add details to, select Details, then do any of the following:

Add a note: Type a description or other information in the text field.

Receive an alert on a specific day: Select “On a day,” then set the date and time you want to be reminded. Select the Never Repeat pop-up menu, then choose a reminder interval.

Assign a priority: Select the Priority pop-up menu, then choose an option. Prioritized items appear with one, two, or three exclamation points in the reminder list.

Delete a reminder

WARNING: When you delete a reminder, it’s deleted on every device with Reminders turned on in iCloud settings. If you’re using updated reminders and delete a reminder with subtasks, the reminder and all its subtasks are deleted.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the list where the reminder appears, then select the reminder you want to delete.

Do one of the following:

Tap or press the Delete or Backspace key.

If you’re not using updated reminders, you can also select Details, then select Delete in the Details window.

Note: If you accidentally delete reminders and you’re not using updated reminders, you can restore an archived version of your reminders. See Restore your reminders on iCloud.com.

Add and delete reminder lists on iCloud.com

All reminders you create are put into a reminder list. Organizing reminders into lists makes it easy to keep your work, personal, and other to-do items separate from each other. Each list contains a place for active reminders and one for completed reminders. See Mark a reminder as completed on iCloud.com.

Create a new list

If you’re using updated reminders, use the Reminders app on a device with iOS 13, iPadOS 13, macOS 10.15, or later to create a new list.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select Add List in the bottom-left corner of the sidebar, below the reminder lists.

Type a name for the list.

Choose a color and an icon or emoji to customize the list, then select Done.

Rename a list or change its appearance

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do either of the following:

If you’re using updated reminders, select the reminder list and select  to the right of the list name. In the pop-up menu, choose Show List Info. Change the name, color, or icon, then select Done.

If you’re not using updated reminders, select the reminder list and select Options next to the list name. Change the name or the list color, then select Done.

Delete a list

WARNING: When you delete a reminder list, the list is deleted on every device with Reminders turned on in iCloud settings. All the reminders it contains are also deleted.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the reminder list you want to delete.

Select  to the right of the list name, then choose Delete List.

Note: If you accidentally delete reminder lists and you aren’t using updated reminders, you can restore an archived version of your reminders. See Restore your reminders on iCloud.com.

Show or hide reminder lists in a group

If you’re using updated reminders, you can organize reminder lists into groups. You can see these groups on iCloud.com. However, you must use the Reminders app on a device with iOS 13, iPadOS 13, macOS 10.15, or later to create and manage them.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the group name to show all reminder lists in the group.

Select the group name again to hide the reminder lists.

Mark a reminder as completed on iCloud.com

Every reminder list includes a section for completed reminders. When you mark a reminder as completed, it appears in the completed section the next time you open the list.

Mark a reminder as completed

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the list that contains the reminder, then select the circle to the left of the reminder.

If you’re using updated reminders, note the following:

If you mark a reminder with subtasks as completed, the subtasks are also marked as completed.

If you mark a subtask as completed, the completed subtask appears below the active subtasks the next time you open the list and have completed tasks showing.

Mark a reminder as not completed

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select the list that contains the reminder.

If you don’t see the reminder you want to mark as not completed, see View completed reminders.

Select the circle to the left of the completed reminder.

If you’re using updated reminders, note the following:

If you mark a reminder with subtasks as not completed, all the subtasks are also marked as not completed.

If a reminder is marked as completed and you mark a subtask as not completed, you need to view completed reminders to see the subtask.

View completed reminders

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Do one of the following:

If you’re using updated reminders, select the list that contains the completed reminder. Select  to the right of the list name, then choose Show Completed.

Completed reminders appear below active reminders.

If you’re not using updated reminders, select the list that contains the completed reminder. Select [number] Completed above the reminder list to see the completed reminders.

Restore your reminders on iCloud.com

You can restore your reminders and reminder lists (together with your calendars and events) from an earlier version that was automatically archived in iCloud.

Note: If you have shared reminder lists, all sharing information is removed when you restore them. You have to share your reminder lists again, and ask other people to reinvite you to share their reminder lists.

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

If you don’t have shared reminder lists, go to the next step.

If you do have shared reminder lists, write down which ones you’re sharing, who you invited to share each one, and whether each participant can view and edit or only view. Also note which reminder lists other people are sharing with you.

Select  in the toolbar, then select Data Recovery.

Select Restore Calendars and Reminders.

Available versions are listed by the date and time they were archived.

To the right of the version you want to restore, select Restore.

There may be more versions than can be displayed. Scroll to see them all.

Note: Wait until iCloud finishes restoring your reminder lists before you change them. During the restore process, any changes you make aren’t saved.

If you had shared reminder lists, reshare them and ask other people to reinvite you to share their reminder lists and calendars. See Share a reminder list on iCloud.com.

The restored reminders and reminder lists appear on all your devices with Reminders turned on in iCloud settings.

If you change your mind, you can restore the reminders and reminder lists you were using. Just follow the steps above to restore the most recent version available.

Share a reminder list on iCloud.com

You can share reminder lists with other iCloud users. Only the owner of a shared list can add and delete people who are sharing the list.

People you share a list with can view the list, mark reminders as completed, add and delete reminders, and see who else is sharing the list.

Note: If you’re using updated reminders, you might not see all of your shared lists on iCloud.com. You also can’t manage sharing on the web. Use the Reminders app on a device with iOS 13, iPadOS 13, macOS 10.15, or later to see and manage all your shared lists.

Share a list or add new participants

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  next to the reminder list.

Type the contact names or email addresses of the people you want to share with.

Select Done.

All invitees receive an email invitation, which they must accept to view and edit the shared list.

Stop sharing a list

Go to icloud.com/reminders, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  next to the shared reminder list.

Select the participant you no longer want to share with, then choose Remove Person. Repeat for each participant you want to remove.

To stop sharing the list, delete all participants.

Deleting a shared list makes it unavailable to everyone, including you.

Resend invitations

Two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication is an extra layer of security for your Apple Account designed to ensure that you’re the only person who can access your account, even if someone knows your password.

You can turn on two-factor authentication and manage your trusted devices and phone numbers by signing in to your Apple Account website. If you create a new Apple Account on a device with iOS 13.4, iPadOS 13.4, macOS 10.15.4, or later, your account automatically uses two-factor authentication.

Enroll in two-factor authentication

If your account meets all the requirements for two-factor authentication, you are prompted to turn it on when you first use your device.

Important: If you’re using two-step verification, you must turn it off before you can turn on two-factor authentication. To do so, sign in to the Apple Account website. In the Security section, click Edit, then click Turn Off Two-Step Verification. You’re asked to create new security questions and verify your date of birth. You should receive an email confirming that two-step verification for your Apple Account is turned off.

Use two-factor authentication

After you’re enrolled, when you enter your Apple Account password for the first time on a new device, you’re asked to verify your identity with a six-digit verification code. This code is displayed automatically on your other devices or sent to a phone number you trust. Just enter the code to sign in and access your information on your new device.

You won’t be asked for a verification code again on that device unless you sign out of your device completely, erase your device, or need to change your password for security reasons.

As extra protection for your Apple Account against phishing attacks, you can use a physical security key instead of a verification code. See the Apple Support article About security keys for Apple Account.

See the Apple Support article Two-factor authentication for Apple Account.

Restore your Safari bookmarks on iCloud.com

You can restore your Safari bookmarks from an earlier version that was automatically archived in iCloud. For example, you might want to restore an earlier version to recover some bookmarks that were accidentally deleted.

When you restore an earlier version, your current version is first archived in iCloud so if you change your mind, you can go back to it.

Go to icloud.com/recovery, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Tip: If you’re already on iCloud.com, you can also select  in the toolbar, then select Recovery.

Select Restore Bookmarks.

You can sort available bookmarks by Date Deleted, Name, or Folder.

To the right of the version you want to restore, select Restore.

There may be more versions than can be displayed. Scroll to see them all.

Note: Wait until iCloud finishes restoring your Safari bookmarks before you change them. During the restore process, any changes you make aren’t saved.

The restored bookmarks appear on all your devices that have Safari turned on in iCloud settings.

If you change your mind, you can restore the Safari bookmarks you were using. Just follow the steps above to restore the most recent version available.

Import emails from another account into iCloud Mail

After you create a primary email address for iCloud Mail, you can import emails from another account, such as Gmail, Yahoo, or Outlook, into your iCloud Mail account. You can then see them in the Mail app and on iCloud.com.

On your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > iCloud.

If you imported emails before, tap Import from Another Address first.

Import emails on iCloud.com

Go to icloud.com/mail, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  at the top of the Mailboxes list, then choose Settings.

Select Import Messages in the sidebar, then select Import.

Select “Choose a provider,” choose an option, then select Continue.

Follow the onscreen instructions.

If you want to import emails to your custom email address, see Import existing emails to your custom iCloud Mail address on iCloud.com.

What are email aliases in iCloud Mail?

An email alias is an alternate email address. It’s like a nickname and helps to keep your real email address private. After you set up a primary iCloud Mail address, you can create up to three @icloud.com email aliases.

After you create an alias, you can send and receive mail from that alias on iCloud.com and on any device that has Mail turned on in iCloud settings. When you send emails using an alias, your email address isn’t shown to the recipients. By default, emails sent to an alias appear in your primary inbox.

Aliases can’t be changed, transferred, or converted to primary accounts. You can delete an email alias at any time. If you have three email aliases and you delete one, you must wait 7 days before you can create a new one.

Note: If you had five MobileMe email aliases when you moved your account to iCloud, you retain the five aliases. However, if you delete one of your five aliases, you can’t create a new one to replace it.

What is a digitally signed and encrypted email?

Email messages that are digitally signed or encrypted can offer enhanced security. You can send or receive signed and encrypted email in the Mail app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

What is a digitally signed email?

A digital signature verifies the authenticity of an email. In other words, it proves that the email was sent from the address it claims to be sent from and that its contents haven’t been altered. When a message is signed, a signed icon  is shown next to the sender’s address.

What is an encrypted email?

Encryption offers an even higher level of security than a digital signature. It allows for private communication between the sender and the recipient that can’t be read or accessed by third parties. When an email is encrypted, a lock  is shown next to the sender’s address.

Note: Some email clients, including the iCloud.com web mail app, may not be able to display encrypted emails.

Share files and folders in iCloud Drive on iCloud.com

You can use iCloud Drive to share files and folders with others so you can collaborate on projects together. The people you invite can download the shared items from iCloud to any of their devices, where they can view them and—depending on the privileges you set—collaborate. You can see any updates the next time you open the files on iCloud.com.

Go to icloud.com/iclouddrive, then sign in to your Apple Account (if necessary).

Select  next to the file or folder you want to share, then choose Share. (On a computer, hold your pointer over the file or folder until  appears.)

Choose who can access the file or folder:

People you choose: Allow only people you invite to access the file or folder. If you select the checkbox next to Access Requests, the first person to visit the link is given access, then anyone else with the link can ask you for access.
